description:
Footage of games, anime, animation and films can now be covered even when nothing names it, `Not this` moved to where it can be judged, and the "videos with no caption" option is gone. Nothing in this release has run in X, YouTube or Instagram, on an emulator or on a phone: the Android changes were unit-tested and compiled only, and the footage check was measured on YouTube frames only.

## Downloads

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `spolierblock-0.2.6-firefox.zip` | Browser extension for Firefox-family browsers. |
| `spolierblock-0.2.6-chrome.zip` | Browser extension for Chromium browsers. |
| `patches-0.2.6.mpp` | Morphe patch bundle for YouTube, X and Instagram. |
| `spolierblock-companion-0.2.6.apk` | Optional Android companion app (one shared list). Update it together with the patched apps. |
| `SHA256SUMS.txt` | Checksums. |

No YouTube, X or Instagram APKs are distributed.

## What changed

- **Unidentified footage.** The setting "Cover unrecognised film, show and game footage" (off by default, formerly "Cover unrecognised film and game images") now also covers video frames and images that look like footage of a game, an anime, an animation or a film when nothing names the work. It judges the picture, not the caption, so a clip posted under an unrelated caption is covered too. It never says which work it is, and it also covers footage of works you have finished unless the post names one you marked seen. It is one small layer on the picture model that was already shipped: no extra download size to speak of, no extra memory.
- **`Not this` only after you have seen the post.** A cover now has `Show once`, `I've seen it` and the settings button. `Not this` is on the pill a post keeps after `Show once`.
- **"Cover videos with no caption" is removed**, on both platforms. It judged a post by what it did not say: it covered unrelated videos and missed footage under an unrelated caption. An older config or export file that still has the setting is accepted and the setting is dropped.

## How well the footage check works

Measured on 20,527 frames of YouTube video (137 works, 101 real-life videos of 83 kinds), each frame judged by a version that never saw its work or its video:

| Kind | Frames flagged | Videos flagged within 30 seconds |
|---|---|---|
| Games | 77 % | 104 of 111 |
| Anime | 77 % | 14 of 14 |
| Animation | 65 % | 16 of 17 |
| Live-action films and series | 32 % | 26 of 38 |
| Real-life video and photos (wrongly) | 0.5 % | 3 of 101 |

An earlier version, scored on 122 clips fetched after it was trained, flagged 36 of 37 game videos within 30 seconds and 2 of 36 real-life ones.

## Known limits

- The footage check is not at 95 %. Live-action is caught in about a third of its frames, so a film scene is often covered late or not at all.
- Sports and simulation games look like broadcasts or the real thing and are hardly caught (FIFA 23, NBA 2K25, EA Sports FC 25, Madden NFL 25, F1 24, Cities: Skylines). GTA VI, left out of training as a whole, was flagged in 45 % of its frames.
- Film-like adverts and music videos are covered as if they were films.
- Which game or film a frame is from cannot be told from the picture: a second picture model (DINOv2) was tried and recognised no more than the shipped one, about 5 to 7 % of frames.
- All figures are from YouTube frames at 360p. X and Instagram video, Android's captured frames and real feeds were not measured.
- The limits listed for 0.2.5 still apply.

release_notes:
Fixes from running 0.2.2 on a real phone. The Android changes in this release have run only on the emulator and in the demo app.

## Downloads

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `spolierblock-0.2.3-firefox.zip` | Browser extension for Firefox-family browsers. |
| `spolierblock-0.2.3-chrome.zip` | Browser extension for Chromium browsers. |
| `patches-0.2.3.mpp` | Morphe patch bundle for YouTube, X and Instagram. |
| `spolierblock-companion-0.2.3.apk` | Optional Android companion app (one shared list). |
| `SHA256SUMS.txt` | Checksums. |

No YouTube, X or Instagram APKs are distributed.

## What changed

- **A bare name means the closest works.** "Minecraft" is the game, "Half-Life" the 1998 game, "Assassin's Creed" the 2007 game and the 2016 film. Sequels and spin-offs are named by their own titles; a type word narrows it ("the Minecraft movie"). Franchise names such as "Halo" and "Star Wars" still take their series.
- **"More from this series" in the picker.** The catalog now records which series each work belongs to (from Wikidata), so "Which have you seen?" can list the rest of a franchise: all 42 Resident Evil works, 13 Silent Hill, 9 God of War.
- **"Show once" stays shown.** It is remembered for the post, not for the view that draws it, so a ticking like counter or a late picture verdict no longer covers the post again.
- **Fewer false covers:** everyday words beside a title that is already matched ("No Damage" in a Devil May Cry video), music titles ("ft.", "official video"), a hashtag alone, and numbers in a video's duration no longer match.
- **Better recall:** plain sentences about well-known multi-word titles ("Resident Evil is scary", "Dark Souls is hard") match again, and "Battlefield Games" style titles match the series.
- **Android**
  - The video being watched on YouTube is no longer blacked out or muted when a covered row scrolls under the player.
  - Covers only draw and take taps where their row is visible.
  - YouTube's duration, view-count and button text is removed before matching.

## Known limits

- Some franchise names resolve oddly: "Call of Duty" means only the 2003 game, "Pokémon" only the 1997 anime, "Harry Potter" the books and the 2026 series but not the films.
- The picker does not open for a name that means a single work, so the series list is not offered there.
- Some well-known titles still need a media word nearby ("The Ring", "The Office", "Metal Gear", "Knives Out").
- A game or film is not identified from footage or pictures that carry no text.
- YouTube comments on Android are not covered.
- "Show once" on Android and the YouTube player fix were verified in the demo and on a logged-out emulator, not in X or on a phone.

Benchmarks and details: README and `docs/`.
